Three named passage reference geometries around Anholt

metadata.goal: Analyze vessel movement patterns around the island and investigate differences in route use.
metadata.category: Anholt island passage geometry and vessel-characteristic differences
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed Danish AIS-style case with 60 complete trajectories on three recurrent passages around Anholt in Kattegat. Static vessel dimensions and separate route/island reference tables support route-use comparisons without exposing route labels in the trajectory table.
metadata.source_note: The case uses Danish AIS-style fields and the real geographic setting of the Danish island of Anholt; all visible trajectories are constructed derived data.

insight_list.insight: Vessel traffic around the island is organized into three main passage routes.

plot.title: Three Complete Passages around Anholt
plot.description: Complete through-trajectories extend beyond the three sides of the passage structure surrounding Anholt.

insight_list.question: What are the main vessel-movement routes around the island?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare complete trajectory geometry with the three supplied passage references.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
points=pd.read_csv(dataset_path); refs=pd.read_csv(Path('route_references.csv')); island=pd.read_csv(Path('island_reference.csv'))
print(refs.groupby('route_name').size()); print(island)

insight_list.insight: Two of the three main routes show a stable speed distribution and a consistent direction of travel, while the other shows a smooth change of direction.

plot.title: Speed Stability and Heading–COG Change by Passage
plot.description: NW–S and NE–S retain nearly constant heading. NW–NE turns slightly southward, then northward and returns close to its entry direction, while COG follows Heading throughout.

insight_list.question: How do speed stability and heading/COG profiles differ among the three passages?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Orient trajectories to a common route direction, normalize trip progress, and compare Heading and COG deviations and their recovery toward the entry direction.

insight_list.insight: Larger vessels are more likely to travel on the northwest–northeast route, while smaller vessels are more likely to travel on the other two routes.

plot.title: Vessel Length and Width by Island Passage
plot.description: Length–width scatter and their footprint proxy show overlapping, probabilistic size differences without assigning small/large labels.

insight_list.question: How are vessel length and width jointly associated with passage choice around the island?

summary: Vessel traffic around the island is organized into three main passage routes. Two of the three main routes show a stable speed distribution and a consistent direction of travel, while the other shows a smooth change of direction. Larger vessels are more likely to travel on the northwest–northeast route, while smaller vessels are more likely to travel on the other two routes.
